title: Financial Accounting II
source_note: Standard NUC-aligned Nigerian university 300L Financial Accounting II curriculum, building on ACC201 (Financial Accounting I): company accounts (share and debenture issues, forfeiture/reissue, redemption), partnership admission/dissolution and goodwill, branch/departmental/consignment/joint venture accounts, royalty accounts, hire purchase accounting, cash flow statements (IAS 7), earnings per share, and accounts of non-trading organisations. Distinct from ACC401 (Advanced Financial Accounting), which covers group/consolidated accounts and business combinations.

questions.question: The maximum amount of share capital a company is authorised by its constitutional documents to issue is called its:
options: Authorised (nominal) share capital
Issued share capital
Called-up share capital
Paid-up share capital
questions.correct_answer: Authorised (nominal) share capital
questions.explanation: Authorised share capital is the ceiling amount of capital a company may issue as stated in its memorandum/constitutional document; issued, called-up and paid-up capital are all subsets of it.

questions.question: 'Called-up capital' that has not yet been paid by shareholders is shown in the accounts as:
options: Calls in arrears
Calls in advance
Share premium
Forfeited shares
questions.correct_answer: Calls in arrears
questions.explanation: Calls in arrears represents the amount a company has called up on its shares but which shareholders have not yet paid.

questions.question: A company issues 100,000 ordinary shares of ₦1 each at a premium of ₦0.50 per share, and the issue is fully subscribed and paid. The total amount received by the company is:
questions.explanation: Total received = number of shares x issue price = 100,000 x (₦1.00 + ₦0.50) = ₦150,000.

questions.question: Under the Companies and Allied Matters Act, the share premium account may lawfully be used to do all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Pay a cash dividend to ordinary shareholders
Write off the company's preliminary (formation) expenses
Issue fully paid bonus shares to existing members
Provide the premium payable on redemption of debentures
questions.correct_answer: Pay a cash dividend to ordinary shareholders
questions.explanation: Share premium is a capital reserve with restricted uses (writing off formation expenses, discount/commission on share or debenture issues, premium on redemption, and bonus issues); it cannot be distributed as an ordinary cash dividend.

questions.question: A company forfeited 500 ordinary shares of ₦1 each on which ₦0.75 per share had been paid, for non-payment of the final call of ₦0.25 per share. The shares were later reissued as fully paid at ₦0.60 each. The amount transferred to capital reserve is:
questions.explanation: The Forfeited Shares account holds ₦375 (500 x ₦0.75) received before forfeiture. The discount on reissue of ₦200 (500 x (₦1.00 - ₦0.60)) is debited against it, leaving ₦375 - ₦200 = ₦175 to transfer to capital reserve.

questions.question: A company with 4,000,000 ordinary shares in issue, currently trading at ₦5.00 per share, makes a rights issue of 1 new share for every 4 held at ₦4.00 per share. The theoretical ex-rights price per share is:
questions.explanation: Total value after the rights issue = (4,000,000 x ₦5.00) + (1,000,000 x ₦4.00) = ₦24,000,000, divided by the new total of 5,000,000 shares = ₦4.80 per share.

questions.question: A bonus (scrip) issue of shares to existing shareholders is financed by:
options: Capitalising reserves such as share premium or retained earnings, with no new cash received
Cash paid in by the existing shareholders
A fresh loan from the company's bankers
Reducing the company's authorised share capital
questions.correct_answer: Capitalising reserves such as share premium or retained earnings, with no new cash received
questions.explanation: A bonus issue converts existing reserves into issued share capital and is given free to existing shareholders in proportion to their holding; no cash is received by the company.

questions.question: A company redeems ₦500,000 of 10% debentures at a premium of 5%. The total amount payable to the debenture holders is:
questions.explanation: Amount payable = nominal value x (1 + premium rate) = ₦500,000 x 1.05 = ₦525,000.

questions.question: The key difference between cumulative and non-cumulative preference shares is that, for cumulative preference shares:
options: Any unpaid dividend accumulates and must be paid in a later year before ordinary dividends can be paid
The dividend rate increases each year automatically
Dividends are always paid before those on non-cumulative preference shares of the same company
They carry full voting rights while non-cumulative shares do not
questions.correct_answer: Any unpaid dividend accumulates and must be paid in a later year before ordinary dividends can be paid
questions.explanation: On cumulative preference shares, arrears of unpaid dividend carry forward and must be settled in full, along with the current year's dividend, before any dividend can be paid to ordinary shareholders.

questions.question: A company has ₦1,000,000 of 10% cumulative preference shares and has paid no dividend on them for the past 2 years. The arrears of preference dividend now owed is:
questions.explanation: Arrears = annual dividend x number of years unpaid = (10% x ₦1,000,000) x 2 = ₦200,000.

questions.question: When preference shares are redeemed wholly or partly out of distributable profits rather than out of a fresh issue of shares, the company is required to transfer an equivalent amount to a:
options: Capital redemption reserve
General reserve
Revaluation reserve
Debenture redemption fund
questions.correct_answer: Capital redemption reserve
questions.explanation: The capital redemption reserve maintains the company's capital base when shares are redeemed out of profits instead of new capital, and it can only be used later for a bonus issue.

questions.question: A company redeems ₦200,000 of preference shares out of distributable profits, partly financed by a fresh issue of ordinary shares raising ₦50,000. The amount that must be transferred to the capital redemption reserve is:
questions.explanation: The transfer to capital redemption reserve equals the nominal value redeemed less the proceeds of any new shares issued to fund the redemption: ₦200,000 - ₦50,000 = ₦150,000.

questions.question: A fee paid to a financial institution that agrees to buy any shares in a new issue that are not taken up by the public is called:
options: Underwriting commission
Brokerage
Share premium
Debenture interest
questions.correct_answer: Underwriting commission
questions.explanation: Underwriting commission compensates the underwriter for guaranteeing that the full issue will be subscribed, by agreeing to take up any shortfall.

questions.question: A convertible debenture (loan note) is one that:
options: May be converted into ordinary shares of the company at a future date on agreed terms
Must always be redeemed in cash at maturity
Carries no fixed rate of interest
Can only be issued to existing ordinary shareholders
questions.correct_answer: May be converted into ordinary shares of the company at a future date on agreed terms
questions.explanation: A convertible debenture gives the holder the option to convert the debt into a stated number of ordinary shares instead of receiving cash redemption.

questions.question: A partnership's average annual profit is ₦60,000, its capital employed is ₦400,000, and the normal rate of return in the industry is 10%. Using the super-profit method with 2 years' purchase, the value of goodwill is:
When a new partner is admitted, the 'sacrificing ratio' is the ratio in which:
options: The old partners give up (surrender) part of their profit share in favour of the new partner
Profits are shared among all partners after admission
Losses are shared between the new and old partners
Capital is contributed by each partner
questions.correct_answer: The old partners give up (surrender) part of their profit share in favour of the new partner
questions.explanation: The sacrificing ratio measures how much of their old profit share each existing partner gives up to accommodate the new partner's share, calculated as old ratio minus new ratio.
questions.topic: Partnership accounts - admission of a partner

questions.question: The rule in Garner v Murray, applied in the absence of a partnership agreement on the point, provides that a deficiency on an insolvent partner's capital account on dissolution should be borne by the solvent partners in the ratio of:
options: Their capitals as last agreed (before dissolution)
Their profit and loss sharing ratio
Equal shares regardless of capital
Their drawings during the final year
questions.correct_answer: Their capitals as last agreed (before dissolution)
questions.explanation: Garner v Murray holds that a deficiency of an insolvent partner is a capital loss to be shared by the solvent partners in proportion to their last agreed capital balances, not their profit-sharing ratio.

questions.question: On the admission of a new partner, any profit arising on the revaluation of partnership assets and liabilities is credited to the:
options: Old partners' capital accounts in their old profit-sharing ratio
New partner's capital account only
All partners' capital accounts in the new profit-sharing ratio
Partnership's general reserve only
questions.correct_answer: Old partners' capital accounts in their old profit-sharing ratio
questions.explanation: Revaluation gains and losses belong to the period before the new partner joined, so they are shared only among the old partners in their old profit-sharing ratio.

questions.question: The main purpose of the 'stock and debtors' system of branch accounting is to:
options: Enable head office to ascertain the branch's gross profit and control branch stock centrally
Avoid the need for the branch to keep any accounting records at all
Record only the branch's cash transactions
Replace the need for a branch profit and loss account
questions.correct_answer: Enable head office to ascertain the branch's gross profit and control branch stock centrally
questions.explanation: Under the stock and debtors system, head office maintains memorandum stock, debtors and adjustment accounts for the branch, which allows it to determine branch gross profit and keep tight control over branch stock and debtors.

questions.question: Goods sent by head office to a branch but not yet received by the branch at the year end (goods in transit) should be treated, in the combined balance sheet, as:
options: Stock in transit, shown as an asset of the business as a whole
A liability of the branch to head office
Written off as a loss immediately
Excluded entirely until received
questions.correct_answer: Stock in transit, shown as an asset of the business as a whole
questions.explanation: Goods dispatched but not yet received still belong to the business, so they are included as stock-in-transit in the combined financial statements to avoid understating assets.

questions.question: In departmental accounts, an expense such as rent, which relates to the premises as a whole, is normally apportioned between departments on the basis of:
options: The floor area occupied by each department
Equal shares regardless of size
Each department's sales revenue only
The number of employees in each department
questions.correct_answer: The floor area occupied by each department
questions.explanation: Rent relates to occupation of space, so the most appropriate and commonly used basis for apportioning it between departments is the floor area each department occupies.

questions.question: A mining lease provides for a minimum rent of ₦50,000 per annum and a royalty of ₦5 per tonne extracted. In a year when 8,000 tonnes are extracted, the short workings arising is:
options: ₦0 (there are no short workings)
questions.explanation: Actual royalty = 8,000 x ₦5 = ₦40,000, which is less than the minimum rent of ₦50,000, so short workings = ₦50,000 - ₦40,000 = ₦10,000.

questions.question: Following the ₦10,000 short workings above, the lease allows short workings to be recouped within the next 2 years. In the following year, royalty based on actual output is ₦65,000 against the same ₦50,000 minimum rent. The amount of short workings that can be recouped that year is:
options: ₦10,000 (the full amount brought forward)
questions.correct_answer: ₦10,000 (the full amount brought forward)
questions.explanation: The excess of actual royalty over minimum rent that year is ₦65,000 - ₦50,000 = ₦15,000, which is more than enough to recoup the full ₦10,000 short workings carried forward.

questions.question: An asset with a cash price of ₦90,000 is acquired on hire purchase for a total HP price of ₦102,000, payable by a deposit and 3 equal annual instalments. Using the sum-of-digits (Rule of 78) method to apportion the total interest of ₦12,000, the interest allocated to the first year is:
questions.explanation: With 3 instalments, the digits sum to 3+2+1=6. The first year, having the highest outstanding balance, is allocated 3/6 of the total interest: 3/6 x ₦12,000 = ₦6,000.

questions.question: The difference between the hire purchase price and the cash price of an asset represents:
options: The interest (finance charge) paid for the privilege of buying on credit
A discount for early payment
Value added tax on the asset
The residual value of the asset
questions.correct_answer: The interest (finance charge) paid for the privilege of buying on credit
questions.explanation: Because payment is spread over time, the buyer pays more than the cash price; that excess is the interest charged by the vendor/finance company.

questions.question: 'Del credere commission' paid to a consignee is additional commission given in return for:
options: The consignee guaranteeing payment from customers, i.e. bearing the risk of bad debts on credit sales
Selling goods at a higher price than instructed
Insuring the goods while in transit
Preparing the consignment account for the consignor
questions.correct_answer: The consignee guaranteeing payment from customers, i.e. bearing the risk of bad debts on credit sales
questions.explanation: Del credere commission compensates the consignee for accepting the credit risk of customers, so any resulting bad debt is borne by the consignee, not the consignor.

questions.question: An abnormal loss of goods on consignment (e.g. due to fire or theft) should be:
options: Valued at cost plus proportionate direct expenses up to the point of loss and charged as a separate loss in the consignor's profit and loss account
Ignored completely since the goods still belong to the consignor
Included in the value of unsold closing stock
Charged entirely to the consignee's account regardless of cause
questions.correct_answer: Valued at cost plus proportionate direct expenses up to the point of loss and charged as a separate loss in the consignor's profit and loss account
questions.explanation: Abnormal losses are not spread over the remaining stock; they are valued on the same basis as stock up to the point of loss and written off separately so as not to distort the normal profit margin.

questions.question: A consignor sends 1,000 units costing ₦200,000, and incurs consignor's expenses of ₦10,000 and the consignee incurs non-recurring expenses (before the goods are put on sale) of ₦5,000. By the year end, 800 units have been sold. The value of the 200 unsold units in closing stock is:
questions.explanation: Total cost loaded onto the 1,000 units = ₦200,000 + ₦10,000 + ₦5,000 = ₦215,000, giving ₦215 per unit. Closing stock = 200 units x ₦215 = ₦43,000.

questions.question: A Memorandum Joint Venture Account is prepared when co-venturers:
options: Each record only their own transactions and do not open a separate set of joint venture books, so a memorandum account is used to combine both sets of records and ascertain the overall profit or loss
Decide to form a registered partnership
Open a joint bank account for the venture
Want to avoid disclosing the venture's profit to each other
questions.correct_answer: Each record only their own transactions and do not open a separate set of joint venture books, so a memorandum account is used to combine both sets of records and ascertain the overall profit or loss
questions.explanation: Where no separate joint venture books are kept, each co-venturer records only their own transactions in their personal books; the memorandum account is a working paper that combines both records purely to compute the venture's total profit or loss.

questions.question: In a statement of cash flows prepared under IAS 7, dividends paid to the company's own shareholders are classified as:
options: A financing activity
An operating activity only
An investing activity
Not shown in the statement of cash flows at all
questions.correct_answer: A financing activity
questions.explanation: Dividends paid to shareholders relate to returns to providers of equity finance and are classified as a financing activity under IAS 7.

questions.question: A company's net profit before tax is ₦80,000, depreciation charged was ₦10,000, trade receivables increased by ₦5,000, inventory decreased by ₦3,000, and trade payables increased by ₦4,000. Using the indirect method, cash generated from operations is:
questions.explanation: Cash from operations = 80,000 + 10,000 (add back depreciation) - 5,000 (increase in receivables reduces cash) + 3,000 (decrease in inventory releases cash) + 4,000 (increase in payables preserves cash) = ₦92,000.

questions.question: A company's profit after tax available to ordinary shareholders is ₦2,000,000, and the weighted average number of ordinary shares in issue during the year is 500,000. Basic earnings per share is:
questions.explanation: Basic EPS = Profit attributable to ordinary shareholders / Weighted average number of ordinary shares = ₦2,000,000 / 500,000 = ₦4.00.

questions.question: A company reports profit after tax of ₦1,500,000, pays preference dividends of ₦300,000, and has 400,000 weighted average ordinary shares in issue. Basic earnings per share is:
questions.explanation: Earnings attributable to ordinary shareholders = ₦1,500,000 - ₦300,000 = ₦1,200,000. EPS = ₦1,200,000 / 400,000 = ₦3.00.

questions.question: A social club received ₦150,000 cash in subscriptions during the year. Subscriptions in arrears were ₦10,000 at the start of the year and ₦8,000 at the end; subscriptions received in advance were ₦5,000 at the start and ₦6,000 at the end. The subscription income to be shown in the income and expenditure account for the year is:
questions.explanation: Subscription income = Cash received + closing arrears - opening arrears + opening advance - closing advance = 150,000 + 8,000 - 10,000 + 5,000 - 6,000 = ₦147,000.

questions.question: For a non-trading (not-for-profit) organisation, the 'receipts and payments account' differs from the 'income and expenditure account' in that the receipts and payments account:
options: Is simply a summary of actual cash and bank receipts and payments, without adjusting for accruals or prepayments
Reports only capital items and excludes all revenue items
Applies accrual accounting to determine surplus or deficit
Is prepared only by profit-making companies
questions.correct_answer: Is simply a summary of actual cash and bank receipts and payments, without adjusting for accruals or prepayments
questions.explanation: The receipts and payments account is essentially a cash book summary, while the income and expenditure account applies the accrual concept to arrive at the period's surplus or deficit, analogous to a profit and loss account.

questions.question: A statement of value added, sometimes included as supplementary information in published accounts, primarily shows:
options: How the wealth created by the enterprise (sales less bought-in materials and services) has been distributed among employees, providers of capital, government and reinvestment
The company's total assets and liabilities at a point in time
The movement in share capital during the year
The company's tax computation in full detail
questions.correct_answer: How the wealth created by the enterprise (sales less bought-in materials and services) has been distributed among employees, providers of capital, government and reinvestment
questions.explanation: A value added statement reformulates profit and loss information to show wealth created and how it is shared among stakeholder groups, rather than showing financial position or share movements.
